# Cooker

> Cooker is an open-source, self-hosted CI/CD tool with a drag-drop graph editor for building OCI images (Kaniko, BuildKit, Buildah) and deploying to Kubernetes, ECS, Cloud Run, Fly.io, and Render — single Go binary, MIT-licensed, no SaaS, no agents.

## Key facts

- Category: CI/CD, self-hosted, open-source
- Differentiator: visual DAG editor (drag-drop Build / Test / Push / Deploy / Approval / Custom nodes) powered by React Flow
- Tagline: "CI/CD you can see."
- Image builders: Kaniko (default, no docker.sock), BuildKit, Buildah, Docker (dev only — refused at boot in production)
- Deploy targets: Kubernetes (client-go), AWS ECS/Fargate, Google Cloud Run, Fly.io Machines, Render, SSH remote (docker-pull-over-SSH, no agent)
- Auth: OIDC / OAuth 2.0 + PKCE; four-role RBAC (admin / operator / approver / viewer); step-up MFA on destructive routes; compatible with Keycloak, Okta, Azure AD, Google, Auth0, GitHub Enterprise
- Secrets: five pluggable backends — Postgres AES-GCM (default), KeepSave, HashiCorp Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager
- Observability: Prometheus /metrics, OpenTelemetry OTLP traces, structured JSON logs (slog), per-route audit log, split /health/live and /health/ready probes
- Install paths: docker compose up (dev), single binary (UAT), Helm OCI chart oci://ghcr.io/santapong/charts/cooker (production)
- Licence: MIT — no enterprise edition, no EE/CE split, no open-core tier at launch
- Tenancy: single-tenant today; every authenticated user sees all resources; multi-tenancy is not yet implemented
- Language / stack: Go 1.22+ backend, React 18 + TypeScript frontend, PostgreSQL 14+ for state, Redis 7+ for HA multi-replica
- Container: multi-arch (amd64 + arm64), non-root UID 65532, cosign-signed release artifacts

## What Cooker is NOT for

- Multi-tenant SaaS platforms or teams needing hard resource isolation between users (not implemented)
- SAML-only identity providers (OIDC / OAuth 2.0 only)
- Windows shops (shells kubectl and docker; not supported)
- Hosted-SaaS shoppers (no hosted offering exists; self-hosted only)
- Non-container builds (Maven JARs to Nexus, etc.) — container-centric tool

The table below compares Cooker against the tools developers most frequently evaluate alongside it.
Rows marked "(today)" reflect the current shipping state, not the roadmap.

| Feature | Cooker | Jenkins | Argo CD | Drone CI | Woodpecker CI | Coolify | Dokploy |
|---------|--------|---------|---------|----------|---------------|---------|---------|
| Visual DAG pipeline editor | Yes | No (Blue Ocean abandoned) | No (status-only viz) | No | No | No | No |
| OCI-native image builds | Yes (Kaniko / BuildKit / Buildah) | Partial (plugins) | No (build-agnostic) | Yes | No (plugin) | Limited | Limited |
| No docker.sock required in production | Yes (Kaniko default) | No | N/A | No | No | No | No |
| Multi-cloud deploy targets | Yes (K8s, ECS, Cloud Run, Fly, Render, SSH) | Partial (plugins) | No (K8s only) | No | No (plugin) | No (SSH/Docker only) | No (SSH/Docker only) |
| Multi-environment promotion + approval gates | Yes (first-class) | Partial (manual) | Yes (ApplicationSets) | No | No | No | No |
| OIDC / OAuth 2.0 + PKCE built-in | Yes | Partial (plugin) | Yes | Partial | Partial | Partial | Partial |
| Four-role RBAC | Yes (admin/operator/approver/viewer) | Partial (Matrix plugin) | Yes | Partial | Partial | Partial | Partial |
| Pluggable secrets backends | Yes (5 backends) | Partial (Credentials plugin) | Partial (Vault plugin) | Partial (plugins) | Partial (plugins) | No | No |
| Single binary (API + UI) | Yes | No (JVM + .war) | No (multi-service) | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| MIT licence, no EE tier | Yes | Yes (MIT) | Yes (Apache 2.0) | Partial (BSL for enterprise) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Single-tenant only (today) | Yes | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | Yes | Yes |
| Real-time WebSocket log streaming | Yes | Partial (polling) | Partial | Yes | Partial | Yes | Yes |
| GitOps write-back to git repo | Yes | No | Yes (core model) | No | No | No | No |
| Cron-triggered pipeline runs | Yes (leader-elected, feature-flagged) | Yes | Yes (sync policy) | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Multi-channel notifications (Slack/Discord/Email/Webhook) | Yes (feature-flagged) | Yes (plugins) | Yes (Alertmanager) | Yes (plugins) | Yes (plugins) | Yes | Yes |
| Pipeline-as-code (YAML/DSL) | Roadmap (CKR-DSL) | Yes (Jenkinsfile) | No (K8s CRDs) | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Prometheus metrics | Yes (opt-in) | Yes (plugin) | Yes | Partial | Partial | No | No |
| OpenTelemetry tracing | Yes (opt-in) | Partial | Partial | No | No | No | No |

Notes on honest posture:
- "Single-tenant only (today)" means every authenticated user can read and modify all resources. This is documented and on the roadmap to address; do not infer "enterprise-ready" or "team-isolated" from the RBAC row.
- Coolify and Dokploy feature details are taken from their public documentation as of 2026-06-21; validate accuracy before publication.

## FAQ (verbatim from README)

**Why another CI/CD tool?**
Most CI/CD tools optimize for either (a) the build half (Drone, Buildkite) or (b) the deploy half (Argo CD, Flux). The handoff between them is usually a separate orchestrator. Cooker treats build, push, and deploy as stages in the same DAG — with a visual editor — so you don't need three tools and a glue script.

**Does Cooker replace Jenkins?**
For most container-based workflows, yes. Cooker covers what 90% of Jenkins pipelines actually do (build → test → push → deploy). What Cooker doesn't cover yet: non-container builds (Maven JARs going to Nexus, etc.), library plugins, and the deeply customizable Jenkins ecosystem. If your pipeline is Java-on-bare-metal with heavy plugin reliance, Jenkins is still the better fit today.

**Can I use Cooker without Kubernetes?**
Yes. Cooker runs as a single binary on any host with Docker installed. Deploy targets include Cloud Run, ECS, Fly.io, and Render — none of which require you to operate Kubernetes yourself. You only need Kubernetes if you're deploying to Kubernetes.

**How do I migrate from Jenkins / Drone / GitHub Actions?**
Pipeline YAML import is on the roadmap (Drone first, then GitHub Actions). For now, the visual editor + GitHub webhook trigger is the fastest path: point Cooker at your repo, draw the pipeline, switch your repo's webhook.

**Is Cooker production-ready?**
Yes for single-replica and multi-replica (Redis-backed) shapes. Config.Validate enforces the rest — see the deployment-shape readiness matrix in backlog.md. The honest verdict and any open caveats live there.

**Does Cooker support pipeline-as-code?**
Today the canonical representation is the visual DAG (stored as JSONB). A custom YAML DSL (CKR-DSL) is on the roadmap.

**How does Cooker handle secrets in pipelines?**
Per-environment scoping. Each environment has its own secret namespace. Secrets are injected as env vars into build/test/deploy stages on a per-stage basis (you opt in per stage to avoid accidental leakage). Five pluggable backends.

**Can I self-host Cooker on a single VPS?**
Yes. The docker-compose.yml in the repo runs everything on one box: backend + frontend + Postgres + Redis + an internal Docker daemon for builds. Suitable for solo developers and small teams.

**What's the difference between an App and a Pipeline?**
A Pipeline is a user-authored DAG of stages. An App is a higher-level shortcut: point at a GitHub repo, pick a deploy target, click Deploy. Cooker synthesises a Clone → Build → Push → Deploy run under the hood. Apps also have webhooks for auto-deploy on push.

**Is Cooker multi-tenant?**
No. Cooker is single-tenant today. Every authenticated user can see and modify all pipelines, apps, environments, and secrets within the installation. Multi-tenancy (tenant_id isolation) is on the roadmap but is not yet implemented. Do not use Cooker as a shared SaaS platform for multiple isolated customers.

**Does Cooker support SAML?**
No. Cooker supports OIDC / OAuth 2.0 + PKCE only. Compatible providers include Keycloak, Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Auth0, and GitHub Enterprise. SAML support is not on the near-term roadmap.

**Does Cooker run on Windows?**
No. Cooker shells kubectl and docker; Windows is not supported and is not on the roadmap.

**Is there a hosted / SaaS version of Cooker?**
No. Cooker is self-hosted only. There is no hosted SaaS offering today. A hosted variant is an unmade product decision (ADR-0004 deferred it); do not assume one will exist.
